subject: Re: Deployment mode selection and migration - Nova Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@nova-health.com>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@nova-health.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode selection & migration — post-call recap + next steps

Thanks for taking the call this morning — good to meet the Nova Health team. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call summary:
- Main goal: migrate from your legacy GPU cluster / self-hosted stack to a production inference platform with predictable latency and lower unit cost.
- Key constraints: EU data residency for PHI-adjacent metadata, sustained throughput (20-30 req/s anticipated), and fast failover for scheduled events.
- Considered deployment modes: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput), Private VPC / on-prem (full data residency + isolation).

Our recommendation (tentative):
- Start with Redwood Dedicated for Phase 1 (predictable throughput, minimal changes to your current API layer).
- Evaluate Private VPC for Phase 2 if you need on-prem or stricter data residency controls for certain workloads.
- Support a hybrid cutover: route low-risk traffic to Dedicated while validating Private deployment in parallel.

Action items / next steps:
1) Please confirm the expected steady-state QPS and peak tokens per request (we discussed ~20-30 req/s, 512–1024 tokens typical).
2) I attached the Redwood Dedicated datasheet and a migration playbook draft — please review.
3) Technical scoping call: propose Vivek (SE) and Laura (Sales Eng manager) join next week to go over network/KMS requirements and timeline.
4) I'll draft a mutual action plan (MAM) and an initial SOW estimate for 1) Dedicated onboarding and 2) Private VPC evaluation.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_datasheet.pdf, migration_playbook.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a call any time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side before the scoping call:

- Residency: we need all customer data to remain in the EU for the initial rollout (production traffic will be EU-only).
- Migration approach: today we have a custom API in front of a legacy GPU cluster and some prompts tuned for the old runtime. Is there a risk that prompt behavior will regress with model/kernel changes?
- Downtime: what's the expected downtime or cutover risk if we move to Dedicated (we need a plan with <30 minutes of disruption if possible).
- Cost: ballpark TCO comparison for Dedicated vs Redwood Hosted vs Private VPC for our volume would help.

I've attached our rough architecture diagram and the RFP doc we shared internally.

Can we schedule the technical scoping on Wed or Thu next week? Vivek included would be great.

Thanks,
Amir Khan
Head of Platform Engineering | Nova Health
amir.khan@nova-health.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection & migration — post-call recap + next steps

Thanks, Amir — great questions. Short answers up front, then we can dive deeper on the scoping call: 

- EU residency: we can provision Dedicated capacity in an EU region and/or run a Private VPC in your EU cloud region; both options meet residency requirements.
- Prompt/regression risk: we test model parity across kernel/quantization paths and provide regression tracking. For critical prompts we run a canary validation set before full cutover; SEs will help calibrate.
- Cutover/downtime: typical pattern is blue/green cutover using DNS & traffic split with a warm KV cache; many customers hit sub-30 minute disruption for the cutover. We'll include fallback policies in the MAM.
- Cost: I'll include a ballpark TCO in the MAM — Dedicated usually wins on steady high-throughput workloads vs Hosted, while Private has additional infra & support line items.

Proposed schedule: Vivek, can you join Wed 30 Jun 09:00 CET (00:00 PDT) or Thu 1 Jul 14:00 CET (05:00 PDT)? We'll tailor to your preferred time.

I'll start a draft SOW for Dedicated onboarding + Private evaluation and share it prior to the call. Attaching migration_playbook.pdf again.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: migration_playbook.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@nova-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection & migration — technical notes

Hi Amir — Vivek from Redwood SE team, thanks for the details and diagram. A few technical notes ahead of the scoping call: 

1) Network & connectivity: for Dedicated we support VPC peering or private interconnects; for Private VPC/on-prem we'll need a maintenance VPN or direct connect + firewall rules. Typical egress rules are minimal but we do require outbound to our patch/update endpoints.

2) KMS & keys: we integrate with customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS/AWS KMS/GCP KMS) and HSMs where required. For Private deployments we can support HSM-backed keys for model keys and token encryption.

3) Migration path options:
   - Lift-and-shift to Dedicated: keep your API layer, point to Redwood endpoints, warm caches and run canary traffic. Minimal code changes required.
   - Hybrid phased cutover: run a subset of models on Dedicated while keeping sensitive workloads on Private.
   - Full Private for on-prem: longer lead time (8–12 weeks typical) for infra and validation, but gives maximum control.

4) SLAs & reliability: Dedicated comes with configurable capacity reservations and auto-fallback policies to ensure availability during node maintenance.

Estimated timelines (rough):
- Dedicated onboarding (capacity provisioning, validation, canary): 4–8 weeks
- Private deployment (infra, networking, validation): 8–12 weeks

Please share the QPS peak and average, typical input/output token counts, and any compliance paperwork timeline (SOC2/audit dates). I'll prepare a short tech appendix for the SOW.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com

- Steady-state QPS: 20–30 requests per second; peak bursts up to ~50 req/s for short windows.
- Typical tokens: 512 input, ~512 output (so ~1024 total) for the user journeys we're prioritizing.
- EU residency: required for production traffic.

Please prepare a draft SOW and ballpark pricing for:
1) Dedicated onboarding (EU region) — quick path for initial cutover.
2) Private VPC evaluation and pilot (EU).

Also please include two references (customers with similar migration stories) and a sample SOC2 evidence checklist. I've attached our RFP (nova_rfp_v2.docx) — can you confirm any additional artifacts you need to respond?

Available for the scoping call Thu 1 Jul 14:00 CET (05:00 PDT) — please send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Amir
